Resolves #20554

A popup observation that leaves its relative placement unchanged now returns without committing an undo step. `Placement` serializes its geometry observations through the existing `lastWrite`, waits for adopted Group writes, and rechecks binding/generation/lifetime before comparing the next hint. Genuine moves, including an out-and-back pair arriving while adoption is queued, remain ordered.

Evidence: L2 producer and mutation controls achieved; the strict rendered witness also passes in a local combined rehearsal. Actual post-merge hosted integration remains required. Residual: AC-4, Residual-Owner: #18379.

| AC-2 | CI-covered: existing free-popup-burst arm still appends one real move. Outside-CI: removing only the equality guard makes the no-op arm fail with identical before/after hints in a new row. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: main-frame rebase, baseline, undo/redo and stale-generation controls remain; queued out-and-back cases cover both an existing hint and initial baseline. An independently admitted Group write is adopted before the next comparison. |
| AC-4 | Post-merge: retain the existing #18379 / PR #20553 owner; rebase the strict witness onto the human-merged fix and pass its hosted Brain tier. Local composition is supporting evidence only. |

## Deltas from ticket

The measured naive one-line guard fixed the no-op but dropped a queued return move: expected `400/220`, observed `460/270`. The [author amended the contract](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20554) to require comparison after queued adoption. The first baseline remains a preserve write; its continuation rechecks current identity before deciding the popup delta.

Change class: `restoration` / `fix`. The producer owns the decision; generic `Transaction.write` semantics are unchanged.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge (non-blocking, a watch item):** the queue-stability loop (`do { await queue } while (queue !== group.queue)`) has no bound. Under sustained Group writes, an observation keeps waiting. Writes are user-driven and observations are already quiesced by `nativeWindowDropSettleMs`, so I expect it to settle. I found no path that keeps the queue busy indefinitely, so this is not a defect.

**Documented search:** I looked for three things and found no concerns:
1. A rejection that could wedge the wait. `group.queue` is chained with `.then(() => {}, () => {})` (`Transaction.mjs:524`), so `await queue` never throws.
2. An unbounded re-entry after the baseline write. `prepare` hands `placementHints` to `captureTopologyPerspective` unchanged (`Persistence.mjs:254`) and throws on validation errors. A successful baseline therefore always adopts the key, and the re-entry runs once.
3. A lifetime gap. `#ingest` re-checks the binding, generation and `isDestroyed` after the await, and checks the Group and `isDestroyed` before it.

The private `#ingest` stops a subclass from replacing the recording body, but a subclass can still replace `ingest` wholesale. Private methods are an established `src` idiom (65 across 24 files), and nothing extends Placement.
